blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Parametric human body models such as the Skinned Multi-Person Linear (SMPL) model provide compact representations of human shape and pose, but their reconstructions remain affected by both errors in estimated latent parameters and limitations in the decoder's expressive capacity. We propose a framework for refining these reconstructions by exploiting the geometric discrepancy between an initial decoded surface and a target mesh, without requiring vertex correspondences between them. The framework comprises three complementary approaches. Latent-VaRefine uses varifold-distance gradients to correct the estimated latent code while preserving the original parametric representation. Vertex-VaRefine processes multiscale varifold-gradient features with a DiffusionNet backbone to predict vertex displacements in a canonical pose, yielding an approximately pose-equivariant refinement pipeline. ElaOpt directly optimizes surface deformations under elastic regularization and normal-direction constraints.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: The accurate capture of 3D deformable objects is commonly done through registration of a given target 𝒯 \mathcal{T} (e.g. a triangular mesh produced by a 3D scanner) onto a 3D mesh with a fixed, canonical mesh topology. For human body shapes, this is most often done by relying on a parametric representation such as the Skinned Multi-Person Linear model (SMPL) ( Loper et al., 2015 ) and its extensions SMPL-H ( Romero et al., 2017 ) and SMPL-X ( Pavlakos et al., 2019 ) . Such a model is given by a latent space ℒ = ℝ N \mathcal{L}=\mathbb{R}^{N} and a decoder Dec ℒ : ℒ → ℝ V × 3 \mathrm{Dec}^{\mathcal{L}}:\mathcal{L}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{V\times 3} which, to a given latent code, associates a triangular mesh with V V vertices. Registration of 𝒯 \mathcal{T} then becomes equivalent to code retrieval , i.e., to finding the latent code whose decoded mesh best represents the target.

blocks.en:
In recent years, many methods for latent code retrieval have been proposed. Optimization approaches such as ( Bogo et al., 2016 ; Pavlakos et al., 2019 ; Kanazawa et al., 2018 ; Feng et al., 2021 ) require heavy user supervision. Learning-based methods, on the other hand, have recently made notable breakthroughs ( Bhatnagar et al., 2020 ) . State-of-the-art frameworks based on equivariant networks such as ArtEq ( Feng et al., 2023 ) have been shown to generalize well to unseen poses. Despite these advances, reconstruction errors can arise from two distinct
sources. First, the retrieval algorithm may fail to identify the parameters
that best explain the observed target, even when its geometry is
representable by the model. Second, the target may contain geometric
details that lie outside the decoder’s representational capacity.
These two sources of error call for complementary corrections:
refining the latent code addresses estimation errors, whereas recovering
geometry beyond the model requires additional surface deformations.

blocks.en:
However, a limitation of all latent code retrieval methods is their inability to retrieve details not representable by the latent space, such as raw scans, or meshes from other, incompatible databases. Hence, a natural question is how to account for these various extra details without losing advantages intrinsic to the parametric model, such as the possibility of animating a human shape, once registered onto the model, through some evolution in the pose parameters of the parametric model. A sufficiently accurate initial reconstruction provides more than an
estimate of the target: it also supplies a structured reference on which
the remaining geometric discrepancy can be represented. This motivates
a residual refinement strategy that uses the reconstructed surface as
a target-adapted reference. The central challenge is to encode and exploit
this discrepancy without requiring vertex correspondences between the
source and target, whose sampling and connectivity may differ.
A further challenge for learned corrections is to account for articulation,
so that similar geometric discrepancies can be processed consistently
across different body poses.

blocks.en:
In this work, we introduce a collection of complementary tools that can be integrated with any latent code retrieval algorithm that produces a decoded surface 𝒮 = Dec ⁡ ( C ) \mathcal{S}=\mathrm{Dec}(C) approximating a target shape 𝒯 \mathcal{T} within a chosen latent representation. Our approaches exploit the geometric proximity between 𝒮 \mathcal{S} and 𝒯 \mathcal{T} to estimate corrections, either in the latent space or directly on the vertices, leading to a corrected surface 𝒮 ^ \hat{\mathcal{S}} capable of recovering finer geometric details of 𝒯 \mathcal{T} . Central to our framework are mesh-agnostic representations of the discrepancies between 𝒮 \mathcal{S} and 𝒯 \mathcal{T} , which allow the correction process to train in a way that remains independent of the topology of the target mesh. For the learning-based approaches, we encode the source–target discrepancy
through varifold-distance gradients, evaluated with respect to either
latent parameters or surface vertices. For vertex-wise prediction,
we additionally express these features in a canonical pose and re-pose
the predicted correction, encouraging approximate consistency across
articulations. The optimization-based approach instead fits the target
directly through a geometric objective regularized by elastic deformation
energies. Together, these mechanisms address different requirements:
preserving the original parametric representation, learning transferable
surface corrections, or refining an individual reconstruction without
training.
Our three main contributions are the following: • Latent-VaRefine: a learning-based method that corrects the latent code C ∈ ℒ C\in\mathcal{L} directly in the latent space, yielding a refined code C + Δ C C+\Delta_{C} . • Vertex-VaRefine: an equivariant, learning-based method that predicts a per-vertex displacement field Δ ∈ ℝ V × 3 \Delta\in\mathbb{R}^{V\times 3} , in which the mesh-agnostic representation is used directly as a per-vertex signal and processed by DiffusionNet. • ElaOpt: an alternative optimization-based strategy relying on a simple elastic energy formulation that deforms 𝒮 \mathcal{S} toward 𝒯 \mathcal{T} while discouraging unrealistic distortions and retaining reposability. A schematic description of these three methods can be seen in Fig. 1 . They may be used individually or in concert, depending on the objective: if retaining a low-dimensional latent code representation is key, then Latent-VaRefine alone may be best. If, instead, simply acquiring accurate, low-noise meshes is the objective, then Vertex-VaRefine may be more practical. Combinations of the methods may also be useful. For example, as will be seen in our results, the strongest improvement in various error measures came from first applying Latent-VaRefine to obtain a better starting point for optimization and then using ElaOpt. These alternatives expose a practical trade-off between preserving
the original model parameterization and increasing geometric flexibility.
Latent-space refinement retains the decoder’s pose and shape
parameterization, whereas vertex-wise refinement introduces additional
degrees of freedom to better approximate the target surface.
The latter retains the source mesh connectivity and can reuse its skinning
structure, but the corrected surface need not correspond to a latent code
of the original model. The appropriate refinement therefore depends on
the representation required by downstream applications, as well as on
reconstruction accuracy.

blocks.en:
We evaluate the proposed refinement methods, individually and in
combination, on AMASS using ArtEq and OmniFit as initial reconstruction
methods. Vertex-VaRefine reduces the mean vertex-to-vertex error of
OmniFit reconstructions from 1.181 to 0.342 cm, corresponding to a
71.0% reduction. Starting from ArtEq reconstructions, combining
Latent-VaRefine with ElaOpt reduces the asymmetric Chamfer distance
from 1.681 to 0.717 cm, a 57.3% reduction. These results illustrate
the complementary strengths of learned vertex refinement for
correspondence accuracy and latent-space refinement followed by
elastic optimization for surface fidelity. Further evaluations
with SMPL-H and SMPL-X demonstrate the adaptability of the framework
to different body models, while experiments on remeshed targets
and raw scans assess its robustness to changes in target
discretization and its ability to refine geometry beyond the
parametric model.

blocks.en: 2 Background and Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 背景和有关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Human Body Latent Spaces
blocks.zh: 2.1 人体后备空间

blocks.en:
Statistical parametric body models constitute the dominant paradigm for low-dimensional human body representation. SMPL ( Loper et al., 2015 ) introduced a skinned linear representation where shape coefficients 𝜷 \boldsymbol{\beta} are obtained by PCA over a population of registered scans, while pose coefficients 𝜽 \boldsymbol{\boldsymbol{\theta}} encode joint-angle rotations driving a linear blend skinning deformation. SMPL was later extended to SMPL-H ( Romero et al., 2017 ) for articulated hands and further to SMPL-X ( Pavlakos et al., 2019 ) for unified body, hand, and facial expression modeling. This was made more sparse in STAR ( Osman et al., 2020 ) . While these parametric models provide a compact and differentiable parameterization, the joint-angle pose space 𝜽 \boldsymbol{\boldsymbol{\theta}} is itself unconstrained: arbitrary parameter values may correspond to implausible meshes. To address this, learned priors over the pose manifold have been proposed, including the VAE-based VPoser ( Pavlakos et al., 2019 ) , the GAN-based adversarial pose prior of Davydov et al. (2022) , and the neural distance field formulation Pose-NDF ( Tiwari et al., 2022 ) .
Yet, the expressive power of the latent space in these approaches remains limited by the model’s parameterization, and any geometry lying outside this manifold, fine surface detail, and clothing cannot be recovered through latent codes alone. In the present work, we will largely make use of the base SMPL model, which is described in more details below. The methods we propose are, however, not specific to SMPL and apply to any latent-space body model, such as SMPL-H and SMPL-X (see Section 10 ).

blocks.en: The Skinned Multi-Person Linear model (SMPL), as introduced in ( Loper et al., 2015 ) and its extensions SMPL-H ( Romero et al., 2017 ) and SMPL-X ( Pavlakos et al., 2019 ) share the same construction. Each consists of latent codes C = ( 𝜷 , 𝜽 ) ∈ ℝ | 𝜷 | × ℝ K × 3 C=(\boldsymbol{\beta},\boldsymbol{\theta})\in\mathbb{R}^{{\left|\boldsymbol{\beta}\right|}}\times\mathbb{R}^{K\times 3} and a decoder that maps any such code to the positions of the V V vertices of a mesh, i.e. an element of ℝ V × 3 \mathbb{R}^{V\times 3} , where the number of vertices V V is fixed for each model ( V = 6890 V=6890 for SMPL and SMPL-H, and V = 10475 V=10475 for SMPL-X). The 𝜷 \boldsymbol{\beta} are shape parameters, the number of which, | 𝜷 | |\boldsymbol{\beta}| , can range up to 300 and is commonly set to 10. The pose parameter vector 𝜽 \boldsymbol{\theta} encodes the relative rotation of each of the K K articulated joints relative to its parent in the kinematic tree, in axis-angle representation, with K = 23 K=23 for SMPL, K = 51 K=51 for SMPL-H (articulated fingers) and K = 54 K=54 for SMPL-X (additional jaw and eye joints). blocks.en: 2.2 Latent Code Retrieval
blocks.zh: 2.2 后端代码检索

blocks.en: Given a target mesh or point cloud, retrieving the latent code that best reconstructs it is a non-trivial inverse problem. Classical optimization-based fitters such as SMPLify ( Bogo et al., 2016 ) and SMPLify-X ( Pavlakos et al., 2019 ) minimize a 2D/3D keypoint-based energy regularized by a pose prior. Regression-based approaches such as HMR ( Kanazawa et al., 2018 ) and PIXIE ( Feng et al., 2021 ) predict SMPL latent codes in a single forward pass from images, while IPNet ( Bhatnagar et al., 2020 ) regresses SMPL latent codes from point clouds via implicit part segmentation. Recently, ArtEq ( Feng et al., 2023 ) introduced an articulated SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \operatorname{SE}(3) -equivariant architecture that generalizes the SMPL fitting to unseen poses by enforcing equivariance in the encoder. VariShaPE ( Hartman et al., 2025 ) proposed an alternative approach via the VariGrad descriptor, a vertex-wise feature that is robust to changes in mesh connectivity and triangulation from ( Hartman and Pierson, 2023 ) . A common limitation persists across these encoders in that they are constrained by the expressive capacity of the underlying body model. The recovered latent code can only describe geometry that lies within the manifold spanned by the decoder. Our work takes a fixed, chosen encoders’ outputs as input and introduces a learned correction module that recovers the residual geometry left out by the latent decoder.
blocks.zh: 由于目标网点或点云,检索最能重建它的潜在代码是一个非三角反向问题. 经典的基于优化的配器,如SMPLife(Bogo等人,2016年)和SMPLify-X(Pavlakos等人,2019年)将2D/3D键位的能量最小化,通过前置姿势进行规范化. HMR(Kanazawa等人,2018年)和PIXIE(Feng等人,2021年)等基于回转的方法预测SMPL潜伏代码从图像中单向传出,而IPNet(Bhatnagar等人,2020年)则通过隐含部分分解从点云中退缩SMPL潜伏代码. 最近,ArtEq(Feng et al., 2023年)引入了一种清晰的SE(3)\operatorname{SE}(3)-等效的架构,通过在编码器中执行等效性,将SMPL配置到不为人知的位置。 VariShaPE(Hartman等人,2025年)通过VariGrad描述器提出了一种替代方法,这一顶点特征对于网格连接和三角化的变化是强有力的(Hartman和Pierson,2023年)。 在这些编码器上存在共同的限制,因为它们受到基本机身模型的表达能力的限制。 恢复的潜伏代码只能描述解码器所覆盖的多面体内的几何. 我们的工作采用固定的、选定的编码器输出作为输入,并引入一个学习的校正模块,以恢复潜在解码器留下的剩余几何特征。

blocks.en: In this section we will present a rigorous mathematical formulation of the latent code recovery problem.

blocks.en: 3.1 Latent Code Recovery
blocks.zh: 3.1 回收新代码

blocks.en: Consider some target mesh 𝒯 \mathcal{T} for which one would like to identify the latent code 𝒞 \mathcal{C} in some latent space ℒ = ℝ N \mathcal{L}=\mathbb{R}^{N} so that the decoded shape 𝒮 = Dec ℒ ​ ( 𝒞 ) \mathcal{S}=\mathrm{Dec}^{\mathcal{L}}(\mathcal{C}) will best approximate 𝒯 \mathcal{T} . Note that, by construction, 𝒮 \mathcal{S} has a fixed mesh topology that is typically determined by the template surface from the decoder, e.g. 𝐌 ¯ \mathbf{\bar{M}} for the SMPL model in Eq. ( 1 ). This generally prevents, outside of artificial examples, the reconstructed 𝒮 \mathcal{S} to match 𝒯 \mathcal{T} exactly and often makes the estimation of the optimal latent code a difficult problem to solve in practice. Further, due to the expressive limits of the latent space and decoder, retaining fine details from the target mesh is typically impossible, even with optimal recovery. Our goal is thus to propose different general strategies for refining estimated latent codes or their corresponding meshes.

blocks.en: In the rest of the paper, the target mesh, which represents the shape to be registered on by the model will always be denoted 𝒯 \mathcal{T} . blocks.en: We propose several strategies which may be combined or used independently to bridge the remaining gap between 𝒮 \mathcal{S} and 𝒯 \mathcal{T} : (1) a method that corrects the estimated latent code C C , and (2) two methods that operate directly on the vertices. blocks.en: 4 The VariGrad representation
blocks.zh: 页:1 VariGrad代表小组

blocks.en: We now recall the definition of the varifold distance and its gradient, VariGrad, which will be an essential ingredient for our learning based approaches. We also explain its equivariant properties and deduce an approximately pose-invariant version of VariGrad. As shown in Feng et al. (2023) , this property allows for better generalization of learned methods, which also translate into requiring a smaller training sample. Indeed, theoretically, with perfect pose equivariance, only training on surfaces with a neutral pose would be required.

blocks.en: The family of reproducing kernel varifold distances originates from the representation of shapes, in particular surfaces, as a specific type of geometric measures known as varifolds. We refer to Kaltenmark et al. (2017) for a more complete introduction to these metrics. The key feature of this distance is its (quasi-)invariance to resampling/re-meshing. The following is only a brief description of how they are computed in practice.

blocks.en: DiffusionNet is a general-purpose architecture for deep learning on 3D surfaces, introduced by Sharp et al. (2022) . Its central idea is that a simple learned diffusion layer provides an effective mechanism for spatial communication across a surface: at each block, per-vertex features are diffused for a learned time scale, so that the spatial support is optimized as a continuous network parameter ranging from purely local to fully global, removing the need to hand-pick neighborhood sizes. Each DiffusionNet block combines this diffusion step with spatial gradient features that support directional (anisotropic) filters and a spatially shared pointwise MLP applied independently at every vertex, and several identical blocks are stacked to form the network. Because diffusion is expressed through intrinsic surface operators (the Laplace–Beltrami operator and mass matrix), which can be discretized on triangle meshes as well as on point clouds ( Sharp and Crane, 2020 ) , the resulting networks are robust to changes in resolution and sampling of a surface. Rather than overfitting to a particular mesh connectivity, the model learns a representation-agnostic solution and can even be trained on one representation, such as a triangle mesh, and evaluated on another, such as a point cloud. This is achieved without any explicit surface convolutions or pooling hierarchies, which makes the architecture simple, efficient, and well suited to our setting.

blocks.en: Finally, we introduce ElaOpt, an optimization-based vertex-wise correction model with regularization based on an elastic deformation energy. The novelty of ElaOpt lies in the combination of three components: (i) a mesh-agnostic elastic registration term rooted in mathematical shape analysis; (ii) restricting the admissible deformations to the surface-normal direction; and (iii) an adaptive mask that enforces stronger regularization in high-curvature or noise-prone regions, such as the face and hands. Given a source shape 𝒮 \mathcal{S} and a target shape 𝒯 \mathcal{T} , we seek a correction field 𝚫 \boldsymbol{\Delta} that minimizes the energy ℰ ⁡ ( 𝚫 ) = ℰ sim ​ ( 𝒮 + 𝚫 , 𝒯 ) + ℰ reg ​ ( 𝒮 , 𝚫 ) . \mathmakebox[c]{\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{\Delta})=\mathcal{E}^{\operatorname{sim}}(\mathcal{S}+\boldsymbol{\Delta},\mathcal{T})+\mathcal{E}^{\operatorname{reg}}(\mathcal{S},\boldsymbol{\Delta}).} The first term, ℰ sim \mathcal{E}^{\operatorname{sim}} , measures the similarity between the corrected source surface 𝒮 + 𝚫 \mathcal{S}+\boldsymbol{\Delta} and the target surface 𝒯 \mathcal{T} , while the second term, ℰ reg \mathcal{E}^{\operatorname{reg}} , regularizes the deformation field 𝚫 \boldsymbol{\Delta} . Note that the regularization term depends not only on the correction vector 𝚫 \boldsymbol{\Delta} , but takes into account the geometry of the source 𝒮 \mathcal{S} . We further emphasize that the correction field is constrained to share the mesh structure of the source surface, whereas the target surface may possess a different triangulation. Consequently, the similarity measure must compare surfaces with non-matching mesh discretizations, as is the case for e.g. the Chamfer distance.

blocks.en: In the following, we provide a high-level description of the chosen energy terms, while full details of the precise energy formulation are deferred to 7.4 . We employ the Chamfer distance to define the similarity energy due to its simplicity and computational efficiency, although alternative geometric shape metrics, such as the varifold distance from Section 4 , could also be used. For the regularization term, we draw inspiration from elastic shape analysis. Specifically, we combine a reparameterization-invariant Sobolev H 2 H^{2} Riemannian metric ( Hartman et al., 2023 ) —defined using the geometry of the source surface 𝒮 \mathcal{S} —with the Square Root Normal Field (SRNF) distance ( Jermyn et al., 2012 ; Kurtek et al., 2011 ; Bauer et al., 2021 ) between the source surface and its vertex-corrected counterpart. An ablation study investigating the influence of the various components of the energy is provided in 9.4 .

blocks.en: 7.1 Baseline Encoder
blocks.zh: 7.1 基线编码器

blocks.en:
As a baseline encoder we employ the state-of-the-art ArtEq model. Since the original ArtEq framework reconstructs meshes with the SMPL male model and is trained on meshes constructed with the male SMPL model, we re-trained ArtEq with the SMPL neutral model to support both male and female body shapes and ensure compatibility with our datasets. To verify that our reported gains do not simply stem from the additional training data used by the two VaRefine models, we also report a second baseline, denoted ArtEq + , which is trained on the same data as the full ArtEq + VaRefine pipeline with the SMPL neutral model.
We emphasize that our methods are not dependent on these specific choices of latent space and encoder, but could be employed on top of any others as well. To illustrate this, we use a converter that maps SMPL codes to corresponding SMPL-H or SMPL-X representations (Appendix B ). It allows us to transpose both the ground-truth codes of the targets and the ArtEq predictions into these other latent spaces, and thus to run the same experiments on those. We also use the very recently proposed OmniFit ( Cai et al., 2026 ) as an alternative choice of baseline encoder to find initial SMPL-X latent codes (Section 10.2 ).
blocks.zh:
作为基线编码器,我们采用了最先进的ArtEq模型。 由于最初的ArtEq框架用SMPL雄性模型重建 meshes,并以雄性SMPL模型构建的meshes进行训练,所以我们用SMPL中性模型重新训练ArtEq,以支持雄性和雌性的身体形状,并确保与我们的数据集兼容. 为了核实我们所报告的成果并非仅仅来自两个VaRefine模型所使用的额外培训数据,我们还报告了第二个基准,即ArtEq +,该基准与全ArtEq + VaRefine管道的SMPL中性模型相同。
我们强调,我们的方法并不取决于潜在空间和编码器的这些具体选择,而是也可以在任何其他选择之上使用。 为了说明这一点,我们使用一个转换器,将 SMPL 代码映射到相应的 SMPL-H 或 SMPL-X 表示(附录 B ). 它使我们能够将目标的地面真实代码和ArtEq预测转换到这些其他潜在空间,从而对这些空间进行同样的实验。 我们还使用最近提出的OmniFit(Cai等人,2026年)作为基线编码器的替代选择,以找到初始的SMPL-X潜在编码(第10.2节)。

In Table 2 we present the computational cost of the proposed refinement frameworks in terms of model complexity and inference efficiency. All experiments were conducted on a machine equipped with an NVIDIA RTX 5000 Ada Generation laptop GPU. For training measurements, the gradient descriptors are assumed to be precomputed. In addition to the reported training cost, the learning based methods required the pre-computation of VariGrad representations for the entire training set. For Latent-VaRefine, where VariGrad representations are computed in the SMPL parameter space using a single scale, this step required 108.48 minutes to compute the descriptors for the full dataset of 89 077 meshes. blocks.en:
Overall, all refinement strategies improve the reconstruction quality across all evaluated datasets, demonstrating strong generalization capabilities across diverse motion distributions and capture conditions. Among the learning-based approaches, Vertex-VaRefine consistently achieves the lowest V2V values. In particular, large improvements are observed on challenging datasets such as GRAB, TCD, and SFU, where Vertex-VaRefine reduces the V2V by up to 57.1 % 57.1\% , 56.4 % 56.4\% , and 52.0 % 52.0\% , respectively.
The optimization based method, ElaOpt, achieves the best Chamfer Distance results across most datasets, with improvements exceeding 50 % 50\% on several benchmarks. Latent-VaRefine already provides a noticeable improvement over the initial ArtEq reconstructions, but remains less accurate than Vertex-VaRefine on both V2V and CD metrics, and than ElaOpt on CD. Its main advantage, however, is that it stays within the SMPL latent space: it outputs refined SMPL parameters rather than a per-vertex displacements, thereby preserving their interpretability. These observations confirm that directly refining the reconstructed geometry at the vertex level leads to more accurate and stable surface corrections than operating only in the latent space, at the cost of leaving the original parametric representation. Finally, we also report results of combining Latent-VaRefine with ElaOpt, by running these two frameworks in succession, which turns out to lead to the consistently best CD results across all data sets and both comparison methods. We also retrain ArtEq on the additional data used in our pipeline (i.e., on DFAUST+BMLmovi), indicated as ArtEq + . Although this does reduce ArtEq’s error, it clearly remains behind Vertex-VaRefine, Latent-VaRefine + ElaOpt, Latent-VaRefine + Vertex-VaRefine applied on top of the original ArtEq, on all sub-datasets, corroborating the fact that the improvement is not explained by the additional training data alone . In addition to these quantitative results, we present in Figure 5 a qualitative comparison, which demonstrates that all proposed methods effectively reduce the per-vertex reconstruction errors across a wide variety of body shapes and poses compared to the initial ArtEq reconstructions.
blocks.zh:
总体而言,所有完善战略都提高了所有已评价数据集的重建质量,显示出在不同的运动分布和捕捉条件中具有强大的概括能力。 在以学习为基础的方法中,Vertex-VaRefine一贯达到最低的V2V值. 特别是,在诸如GRAB、TCD和SFU等具有挑战性的数据集方面观察到了很大的改进,其中Vertex-VaRefine将V2V分别减少了57.1%、56.4%、52.0%和52.0%。
基于优化的方法ElaOpt在大多数数据集中都实现了最佳的Chamfer距离结果,在几个基准上改进了50%以上。 与最初的ArtEq重建相比,Lententnt-Va Refine已经有了显著的改进,但在V2V和CD的衡量标准上仍然不如Vertex-VaRefine准确,在CD上也不如ElaOpt准确。 然而,其主要优势在于它停留在SMPL潜在空间内:它输出精细的SMPL参数而不是一个反向迁移,从而保持其可解释性. 这些观测结果证实,在顶点一级直接改进重建的几何,比仅在潜伏空间运行更准确和稳定地进行表面校正,代价是离开原来的参数化表示. 最后,我们还报告将Latent-VaRefine与ElaOpt合并的结果,办法是连续运行这两个框架,结果导致所有数据集和两种比较方法的CD结果始终最佳。 我们还对ArtEq进行关于我们管线中使用的补充数据(即DFAUST+BMLmovi)的再培训,称为ArtEq+. 尽管这确实减少了ArtEq的错误,但它显然仍然落后于Vertex-VaRefine,Latet-VaRefine + ElaOpt,Latet-VaRefine + Vertex-Va Refine 在所有子数据集上应用的原始ArtEq,这证实了这样的事实,即改进并非仅由额外的培训数据来解释。 除了这些定量结果外,我们在图5中提出了质的比较,这表明所有拟议方法都有效减少了各种身体形状的反向重建错误,并与最初的ArtEq重建相比,呈现了面貌.

blocks.en: 9 Ablation Studies
blocks.zh: 9 读物研究

blocks.en: 9.1 Number of VariGrad Scales
blocks.zh: 9.1 变格号数

blocks.en: We analyze here the contribution of the proposed components through a series of ablation studies. First, we evaluate the impact of the number of VariGrad scales used during refinement. We study the effect of different multi-scale VariGrad configurations on the performance of the Latent-VaRefine and Vertex-VaRefine models. In the latent refinement setting, increasing the number of scales beyond a single-scale representation slightly degrades performance. In contrast, the vertex refinement model benefits from multi-scale VariGrad features with the 3-scale configuration providing the best trade-off between accuracy and stability across the AMASS benchmark and is therefore adopted in the final model.
blocks.zh: 我们在此通过一系列消化研究分析拟议组成部分的贡献。 首先,我们评价在改进过程中使用的VariGrad天平数量的影响。 我们研究不同的多尺度VariGrad配置对Latent-VaRefine和Vertex-VaRefine模型性能的影响. 在潜在的完善环境中,比单一比额表代表制以外的比额表数目的增加略微降低了业绩。 相比之下,顶点完善模型得益于多尺度的VariGrad特性,3尺度的配置为整个AMASS基准的精确度和稳定性提供了最佳的权衡,因此在最终模型中被采用.

blocks.en: For Latent-VaRefine, we consider 3 and 5 scale variants and also perform an ablation to test the value of including the coefficient fidelity term. In addition to the base .75 .75 cm base scale, we include half and double scale ( .375 .375 cm and 1.5 1.5 cm) VariGrad descriptors to obtain a 3-scale VariGrad layer. To these are further added the 5 5 cm and 15 15 cm VariGrads to obtain a 5-scale model. The ablation to test the value of the coefficient fidelity term is performed using the same single .75 .75 cm VariGrad as the standard Latent-VaRefine with the only difference being that only MSE is used for training loss in this case.
blocks.zh: 对于Lententnt-Va Refine,我们考虑3和5个尺度变体,并进行减值测试,以测试包含系数忠诚值的值。 除了基数为.75 .75厘米的基数尺度外,我们还包括半尺度和双尺度(375 375厘米和1.5厘米)的VariGrad描述符,以获得一个3级的VariGrad层. 此外,还增加了5 5厘米和15 15厘米瓦里格拉姆,以获得5级模型。 测试系数忠义值的偏差是使用与标准Latent-VaRefine相同的单值75.75 cm VariGrad进行,唯一的区别是在这种情况下,只有MSE用于培训损失。

blocks.en: The comparison of the standard 1 scale Latent-VaRefine to the 3 and 5 scale versions is found in Table 5 , which also includes the MSE-only ablation results. In all cases, the standard Latent-VaRefine performs best by a slim margin. It is likely that the wider model needed to accommodate the additional input data is the cause of the lower performance of the 3 and 5 scale variants. The inclusion of the coefficient fidelity term appears to improve both MVE and Chamfer error as the term likely both regularizes the training and directly encourages improvement as errors in coefficients lead to higher MVE and Chamfer error.
blocks.zh: 标准1尺度Latent-VaRefine与3和5尺度版本的比较见表5,其中也包括只限MSE的衰减结果. 在所有情况下,标准Latent-VaRefine的性能最好,差幅很小。 容纳额外输入数据所需的更广泛模型很可能是3和5尺度变体性能较低的原因. 列入系数忠义词似乎可以改善MVE和Chamfer的误差,因为该词既有可能使培训正规化,又会直接鼓励改进,因为系数错误导致MVE和Chamfer的误差较高。

blocks.en: Similar to the study on Latent-VaRefine, we wish to determine the potential effect of adding more scales in the VariGrad representation. To that end, we consider multiple uniformly spaced scales in order to capture geometric discrepancies at different spatial resolutions. We thus consider three specific configurations: a single scale {5 cm}, three scales {3 cm, 6 cm, 10 cm}, and five scales {2 cm, 4 cm, 6 cm, 8 cm, 10 cm}. Table 5 reports the reconstruction performance obtained with each configuration using both the vertex-to-vertex (V2V) and the asymmetric Chamfer Distance (CD). These results show that multi-scale VariGrad features consistently improve reconstruction performance over a single scale. Notably, the performance gain between the single-scale and the 3-scale configuration (V2V: 1.734 vs. 1.552 on AMASS) is substantially larger than the performance gain between the 3-scale and 5-scale configurations (V2V: 1.552 vs. 1.527), indicating that most of the benefit of multi-scale VariGrad features is already achieved with 3 scales, with diminishing returns beyond that point. While the 5-scale configuration achieves the best results on most datasets, this additional improvement over the 3-scale configuration is modest and comes at a noticeably higher memory and training-time cost, since each additional scale requires computing, storing, and projecting an extra VariGrad feature channel per vertex. We therefore adopt the 3-scale configuration as our final choice, as it offers the best trade-off between reconstruction accuracy and computational cost.

blocks.en: 9.2 Effect of the Equivariance in Vertex-VaRefine
blocks.zh: 9.2 等离子体对Vertex-VaRefine的影响

blocks.en: Section 6.1 argues that Vertex-VaRefine is approximately pose-equivariant by construction , but not fully equivariant; this is confirmed by Table 1 , with a median relative error of 4 4 – 10 % 10\% and a mean relative error of 23 23 – 50 % 50\% . To determine if this approximate equivariance is genuinely beneficial rather than merely a design choice, we trained an otherwise identical variant that entirely omits the canonical-frame projection and the neutral pose/re-posing step. In this version, the DiffusionNet backbone processes raw, unprojected VariGrad descriptors computed directly on the posed source mesh and predicts displacement directly in posed space, providing no equivariance guarantees. Both variants maintain the same backbone architecture, VariGrad scales, loss functions, and training data; the only difference lies in the pose-equivariant wrapping.
blocks.zh: 第6.1节认为,Vertex-VaRefine通过建筑形式大致相当,但并不完全等同;表1证实了这一点,相对误差中位数为4 4 — 10 % 10 — 和平均相对误差为23 23 — 50 % 50 — 。 为了确定这种大致的等效性是否真正有益,而不仅仅是一种设计选择,我们训练了一个本来完全相同的变体,它完全省略了犬形框架投影和中性姿势/重置步骤。 在这个版本中,DifplusionNet主干线处理原始的、未经预测的VariGrad描述符直接在所显示的源网点上计算,并直接预测在所显示的空间中迁移,没有提供等价保证。 两种变体都保持了相同的主干架构,VariGrad比例尺,损失函数,以及训练数据;唯一的区别在于姿势-等效的包装.

blocks.en: 9.4 ElaOpt Ablations

blocks.en: We perform two ablation studies on ElaOpt. The first is a simple comparison against SMPL+D , and the latter is a term-wise examination, to qualitatively inspect the value of the individual terms and their quantitative impact on reported metrics such as V2V error and Chamfer error.

blocks.en: 10 Generalizability
blocks.zh: 10 通用性

blocks.en: As a final set of evaluation tests, we examine the generalizability of our methods. We show that they work with a different choice of decoder (OmniFit ( Cai et al., 2026 ) ), of latent space (SMPL-H/X), and with targets outside of the reach of the decoder (due to either a change of resolution or belonging to a more general category, such as raw scans).
blocks.zh: 作为最后一套评估测试,我们审查我们方法的通用性。 我们显示,他们的工作选择有不同的解码器(OmniFit(Cai等人,2026年)),潜在空间(SMPL-H/X),以及解码器无法达到的目标(因为分辨率改变或属于更普通的类别,如原始扫描).

blocks.en: 10.1 Generalizability to a different latent space
blocks.zh: 10.1 不同潜在空间的通用性

blocks.en:
To demonstrate that our framework is not specific to SMPL, we apply all three methods (Latent-VaRefine, Vertex-VaRefine and ElaOpt) to two richer body models. SMPL-H shares the SMPL template topology, but articulates the fingers. SMPL-X additionally models the jaw, eyes, and facial expressions. Since ArtEq is trained for SMPL, we do not retrain it for these models.
Instead, the SMPL-H and SMPL-X codes of both the source and target meshes are obtained from the corresponding SMPL codes with the SMPL → \to SMPL-H and SMPL → \to SMPL-X converters of Appendix B : the source codes are converted ArtEq predictions, and the target codes are converted ground-truth SMPL codes. The two learning-based methods are retrained with the SMPL-H/SMPL-X versions of the BMLmovi data, keeping the architectures of Section 7 . In the case of Vertex-VaRefine, hyper-parameters are also kept identical. For Latent-VaRefine the learning rate and relative coefficient-loss/MSE-loss weighting were adjusted. For SMPL-X we set w MSE = 20 w_{\mathrm{MSE}}=20 while for SMPL-H we set w MSE = 1 w_{\mathrm{MSE}}=1 . For both, the initial learning rate was set to 10 − 4.0 10^{-4.0} and an additional weight was needed for the new hand parameters for the latent space loss. As there are 90 hand parameters in SMPL-H and SMPL-X and these parameters have little effect on overall mesh correctness, this weight was set to 0 0 . ElaOpt requires no training and is applied directly to the converted source and target meshes. All methods are evaluated on the remaining AMASS sub-datasets, and are showed to perform similarly well as on their SMPL version.

为了证明我们的框架并非专门针对SMPL,我们把所有三种方法(Latent-VaRefine,Vertex-VaRefine和ElaOpt)都应用到两个更丰富的体型上. SMPL-H共享SMPL模板地形,但表达手指. SMPL-X还模拟了下巴、眼睛和面部表情。 由于ArtEq是SMPL训练的,我们不为这些模型重新训练.
取而代之的是,来源和目标网格的SMPL-H和SMPL-X代码都是从SMPL对应的SMPL代码中获取的,与附录B的SMPL-H和SMPL →\为SMPL-X转换器:源代码转换ArtEq预测,目标代码转换为地面真实SMPL代码. 这两种基于学习的方法与BMLmovi数据的SMPL-H/SMPL-X版本重新训练,保留了第7节的架构. 就Vertex-VaRefine而言,超参数也保持不变。 对于Lententnt-Va Refine,对学习率和相对系数损失/MSE损失加权进行了调整。 对于SMPL-X,我们设定w MSE = 20 w_{\mathrm{MSE}}=20 而对于SMPL-H,我们设定w MSE = 1 w_{\mathrm{MSE}}=1 。 对两者来说,初始学习率定为10-4.0-10-4.0,对于潜在空间损失的新手参数,需要额外加权。 由于SMPL-H和SMPL-X中有90个手动参数,这些参数对整体网格正确性影响不大,因此这个重量被设定为0 0. ElaOpt不需要训练,直接应用到转换的源头和瞄准网格. 所有方法均在其余的AMASS子数据集上评价,并显示其性能类似以及SMPL版本.

blocks.en: 11 Limitations and Future work
blocks.zh: 11. 限制和今后的工作

blocks.en: From the results of the previous sections, one can conclude that Latent-VaRefine preserves the latent representation but is less accurate, though it can be easily combined with the two other frameworks to effect; Vertex-VaRefine achieves the lowest vertex-to-vertex errors; while ElaOpt yields the best Chamfer distances and is extendable to clothed meshes (see Appendix D ), at the cost of a substantially slower inference and potentially more irregular output meshes. Combining a learning based initialization with few subsequent optimization steps is a natural direction for future work. Another common limitation to all proposed methods is the assumption that the source mesh produced by the base latent code retrieval method is not too far from the ground truth, especially in terms of the predicted pose. This could possibly be improved by adapting Latent-VaRefine to capture bigger changes, which we intend to investigate.

blocks.en: In their current form, all three methods allow for animation of the refined shape using the pose parameter of the latent space from which the source shape is obtained. This could be used in conjunction with motion generation algorithms such as ARDY ( Zhao et al., 2026 ) to animate general body shapes. On the other hand, the generation of more general human body shapes using generative methods could be possible, though it will probably require adapting the Vertex-VaRefine approach to allow for a useful latent space on which to work. This is another topic of interest as a natural follow-up to this work.

blocks.en: Appendix B SMPL to SMPL-H and SMPL-X Converters
blocks.zh: SMPL-H和SMPL-X转换器的附录B SMPL

blocks.en: The parameters of SMPL latent codes can be used naively as SMPL-X or SMPL-H parameters. One simply matches up shape ( 𝜷 \boldsymbol{\beta} ) parameters and assigns the pose ( 𝜽 \boldsymbol{\theta} ) parameters of one latent space to the relevant pose parameters of the other. The immediate issue is the simple architectural differences between the different latent spaces. SMPL offers 6 coefficients for hands, but SMPL-X and SMPL-H offer as many as 90, 45 for either hand, if one does not use PCA. SMPL-X adds expression coefficients for the face and parameters for jaw and eye position. Even if one chooses, as a matter of convention, to simply discard hand and expression information and match only the common joints and the shape parameters, the result is not the identity. That is, the exact mesh encoded by a set of shape ( 𝜷 \boldsymbol{\beta} ) and joint ( 𝜽 \boldsymbol{\theta} ) parameters depends on the decoder used even if one restricts to parameters held in common. See Figure 8 for a typical example.

SMPL-X增加了面部的表达系数和下巴和眼部位置的参数. 即使作为惯例,人们选择仅仅丢弃手和表达信息,只匹配常见关节和形状参数,结果也不是身份. 也就是说,用一组形状(β\boldsymbol\beta})和联合(θ\boldsymbol\theta})编码的精确网格参数取决于所使用的解码器,即使一个限制的参数是共同的。 典型的例子见图8。

blocks.en: To avoid retraining ArtEq for SMPL-X or performing long intensive computations to find optimal matchings between the thousands of relevant SMPL and SMPL-X parameters, we resort to training a simple neural network for the task. The fact that makes this workable is that while the meshes encoded by SMPL and SMPL-X by a common set of parameters will differ, they do not differ extremely. The poses are nearly right. Additionally, there is a matrix, which we will here denote ℳ \mathcal{M} , provided by the SMPL(-X) ecosystem to convert a generated SMPL-X mesh into one with the topology of an SMPL mesh. This allows us to train an autoencoder to find parameters correspondences with MSE loss: Loss ⁡ ( C ′ ) = MSE ⁡ ( Dec SMPL ​ ( C ) , ℳ ​ Dec SMPLX ​ ( C ′ ) ) . \operatorname{Loss}(C^{\prime})=\operatorname{MSE}(\mathrm{Dec}^{\mathrm{SMPL}}(C),\mathcal{M}\mathrm{Dec}^{\mathrm{SMPLX}}(C^{\prime})). These losses are computed after an area-weighted centroid based centering, as SMPL and SMPL-X do not have a common center.

blocks.en: Naively attempting to train with the above loss with a single large network appears to be slow and prone to local optima. More effective is to train in three stages. We trained the model to convert SMPL latent codes with 10 shape parameters into SMPL-X latent codes with 10 shape parameters. The SMPL latent code is 82 parameters: 3 parameters corresponding to a global orientation, 63 corresponding to non-hand joints, 6 for SMPL’s simple hand joints, and 10 shape parameters. The SMPL-X latent code is 166 parameters: 3 parameters corresponding to a global orientation, 63 corresponding to non-hand joints, 90 for SMPL-H style hands, and 10 shape parameters. The first stage is a pair of MLPs, one MLP converting the 6 SMPL hand joint parameters into 90 SMPL-H style parameters and one MLP converting the 10 shape parameter from SMPL parameters to SMPL-X parameters. Training this stage alone will find parameters such that the shape will better match than naive parameter matching. The body pose can then be corrected by training an MLP to find a correcting term for the pose parameters. Finally, once both are roughly correct, the end to end combination of the two stages can be trained together for a final performance increase. blocks.en: PoissonNet ( Maesumi et al., 2025 ) is an intrinsic mesh neural network that replaces the spectral diffusion operator of DiffusionNet ( Sharp et al., 2022 ) with a differentiable Poisson equation solving as its mechanism for information propagation across the surface. Given per-vertex scalar features x ∈ ℝ V × C x\in\mathbb{R}^{V\times C} , each Poisson block proceeds in three steps: (i) the intrinsic gradient operator G ∈ ℝ 2 ​ F × V G\in\mathbb{R}^{2F\times V} maps vertex features to per-face tangent-plane gradients, ∇ x = G ​ x \nabla x=Gx , represented as complex numbers in a local 2D basis per face; (ii) a complex-valued MLP transforms these tangent-vector features while preserving the S ​ O ​ ( 2 ) SO(2) -equivariance of the local frame; (iii) a Poisson equation L ​ u = div ⁡ ( A ⋅ grads ) Lu=\operatorname{div}(A\cdot\text{grads}) is solved in closed form via a pre-factorized (Cholesky) cotangent Laplacian L L ( Nicolet et al., 2021 ) – one factorization per mesh, reused across all channels and both forward/backward passes – to obtain a globally smoothed vertex signal u u . The block output is MLP ⁡ ( [ x , u ] ) + x \mathrm{MLP}([x,u])+x . Stacking N N such blocks after a linear input projection gives the PoissonNet backbone; a final linear head maps C width C_{\text{width}} -dimensional vertex features to the task output.

SpiralNet++ ( Gong et al., 2019 ) offers an attractive compromise: it
defines a fast, anisotropic mesh convolution by following spiral sequences of neighbouring vertices on a mesh of fixed topology. In the case where the source shape has a fixed mesh template, like in ours (the source mesh 𝒮 \mathcal{S} is always decoded from a given latent space and therefore has consistent mesh structure), the spirals can be precomputed once and reused across the dataset, leading to an efficient and topology-aware encoder particularly suited to body meshes. The final output then needs to be as detailed as possible, so we forego the usual downsampling of SpiralNet. This lets us directly obtain a per-vertex processed feature z = ( z 1 , … , z V ) ∈ ℝ K × V z=(z_{1},\dots,z_{V})\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times V} . Finally, to prime this code for the next module, we turn it into per-face feature Z = ( Z 1 , … , Z F ) ∈ ℝ K × F Z=(Z_{1},\dots,Z_{F})\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times F} . For each face index f = 1 ​ … ​ F f=1\dots F of the mesh, Z f Z_{f} is the average of the three codes z i ​ s z_{i}s attached to the three vertices of that face.

For DiffusionNet and PoissonNet, the backbone directly outputs the per-vertex T-pose displacement D = Net ⁡ ( ϕ ) ∈ ℝ V × 3 D=\mathrm{Net}(\phi)\in\mathbb{R}^{V\times 3} through a final linear layer, with no further post-processing.
For SpiralNet++, directly regressing D D from per-vertex features produces noisy and spatially inconsistent corrections. To enforce smoothness without sacrificing expressivity, we instead adopt a slightly modified version of the Neural Jacobian Field ( Aigerman et al., 2022 ) formulation on top of the SpiralNet++ encoder. Rather than predicting the displacement directly, the network outputs a per-triangle 3 × 3 3{\times}3 Jacobian matrix J f = MLP ⁡ ( Z f , c f ) J_{f}=\operatorname{MLP}(Z_{f},c_{f}) , f = 1 , … , F f=1,\dots,F , from the per-face encoder features Z f Z_{f} and face centers c f c_{f} introduced above. The columns of J f J_{f} are interpreted as the surface gradient of each coordinate of the T-pose correction. The deformation is then recovered by solving the Poisson system L 𝒮 0 ​ Δ = 𝒜 𝒮 0 ​ ∇ 𝒮 0 T J f , \mathmakebox[c]{L_{\mathcal{S}_{0}}\,\Delta=\mathcal{A}_{\mathcal{S}_{0}}\,\nabla^{T}_{\mathcal{S}_{0}}\,J_{f},} where L 𝒮 0 L_{\mathcal{S}_{0}} is the surface Laplacian, 𝒜 𝒮 0 \mathcal{A}_{\mathcal{S}_{0}} the diagonal matrix of face areas, and ∇ T \nabla^{T} the transpose of the surface gradient operator, all computed once on a fixed reference template 𝒮 0 \mathcal{S}_{0} (the template SMPL mesh) shared by every training sample. Since 𝒮 \mathcal{S} , and hence 𝒮 ¯ \bar{\mathcal{S}} , always share the SMPL topology, this Poisson system is factorized only once, independently of the training set size, which keeps memory and training time tractable. Unlike the original, non-equivariant formulation, the resulting correction Δ \Delta is here added to the per-sample T-pose shape rather than to 𝒮 0 \mathcal{S}_{0} itself, D ≐ Δ D\doteq\Delta with T = 𝒮 ¯ + Δ T=\bar{\mathcal{S}}+\Delta – this is what makes this decoding head compatible with the pose-equivariant pipeline described above. This approach has two advantages: it introduces a regularization prior on the deformation appropriate for body geometry, and it preserves the intrinsic differential structure of the source surface, so fine-scale features are not distorted during refinement.

blocks.en: In a manner similar to SMPL+D and Bhatnagar et al. (2020) , per vertex correction preserves the original joint rigging and skinning weights allowing the reconstruction be reposed or animated. Additionally, unlike methods constrained to the latent space’s representative limits, these vertex corrections can be applied to capture clothing or other details outside the latent space constraints. These are items we will explore in future work, and we present in this section some promising early proof-of-concept efforts.
blocks.zh: 以类似于SMPL+D和Bhatnagar等人(2020年)的方式,每个顶点校正保留了原来的联合装配和剥皮重量,允许重置或动画. 此外,与限制在潜在空间代表性限度内的方法不同,这些顶点修正可用于捕捉潜在的空间限度以外的服装或其他细节。 这些都是我们将在今后工作中探讨的项目,我们在本节介绍一些有希望的早日证明概念的努力。

blocks.en: Figure 12 a-b), presents qualitative reconstructions of scans from the CAPE ( Ma et al., 2020 ) and THuman ( Yu et al., 2021 ) datasets. Starting from minimally clothed SMPL meshes, each method predicts deformation fields that recover the geometry of the target clothed scans. Quantitatively, the Vertex-VaRefine framework reduces the vertex-to-vertex Error (V2V) from 1.74 ​ cm 1.74\,\mathrm{cm} to 1.61 ​ cm 1.61\,\mathrm{cm} , corresponding to a relative improvement of approximately 7.5 % 7.5\% . Meanwhile, the ElaOpt method reduces the V2V to 1.41 ​ cm 1.41\,\mathrm{cm} corresponding to a relative improvement of 19 % 19\% . Qualitatively, VaRefine captures the overall clothing geometry, but not enough to convincingly dress the source mesh. Fine-scale cloth wrinkles and high-frequency surface details remain challenging. ElaOpt on the other hand, yields much better-looking results, both in terms of large scale geometry and wrinkles.
